annotations.title: Defrauded.
annotations.text: In that (ſaith S. Auguſtine) <mn>[1]</mn> he withdrew any part of that which he promiſed, he vvas guilty at once, both of ſacrilege, <mn>[2]</mn>and of fraude. of ſacrilege, becauſe he robbed God of that vvhich vvas his by promes: of fraude, in that he withheld of the whole gift, a peece. Let now the Heretikes come, and ſay it was for lying or hypocriſie onely that this facte vvas condemned: becauſe they be loth to haue ſacrilege counted any ſuch ſinne, who haue taught men not onely to take avvay from God ſome peece of that or al that them ſelues gaue, but plainly to ſpoile & apply to them ſelues al that other men gaue.

notes.text: Aug. ser. 9. in append. de diuersis tom. 10.

annotations.title: Peter ſaid.
annotations.text: S. Peter (as you ſee here) without mans relation knew this fraude and the cogitations of Ananias, and as head of the College and of the whole Church againſt which this robbery vvas committed, executed this heauy ſentence of Excommunication [1] both againſt him, and his vvife conſenting to the Sacrilege. for it was excommunication by S. Auguſtines iudgement, (li. 3 cont. ep. Parm. c. 1 to. 7) and had this corporal miraculous death ioyned withal, as the Excommunication that S. Paul [2] gaue out againſt the inceſtuous and others, had the corporal vexation of Satan incident vnto it.

annotations.title: In thy povver.
annotations.text: [1] If it diſpleaſed God (ſaith S. Auguſtine) to vvithdravv of the money vvhich they had vovved to God, hovv is he angry vvhen chaſtitie is vovved and is not performed? for to ſuch may be ſaid that vvhich S. Peter ſaid of the money: Thy virginitie remaining did it not remaine to thee, and before thou didſt vovv, vvas it not in thine ovvne povver? for, vvhoſoeuer haue vovved ſuch things and haue not paied them, let them not thinke to be condemned to corporal deaths, but to euerlaſting fire. Auguſt. Ser. 10. de diuerſis. And S. Gregorie [2] to the ſame purpoſe vvriteth thus, Ananias had vovved money to God, vvhich aftervvard ouercome vvith diueliſh perſuaſion he vvithdrevv: but vvith vvhat death he vvas puniſhed, thou knovveſt. If then he vvere vvorthy of that death, vvho tooke avvay the money that he had giuen to God, conſider vvhat great peril in Gods iudgement thou ſhalt be vvorthy of, vvhich haſt vvithdravven, not money, but thy ſelf from almighty God, to vvhom thou hadſt vovved thy ſelf vnder the habite or vveede of a Monke.

notes.text: Vovv of Chastitie, & the breache thereof.

annotations.title: Not to men, but.
annotations.text: To take from the Church or from the Gouernours thereof, things dedicated to their vſe and the ſeruice of God, or to lie vnto Gods Miniſters, is ſo iudged of before God, as if the lie vvere made, and the fraude done to the Holy Ghoſt him ſelf, vvho is the Churches Preſident and Protector.

annotations.title: His ſhadovv.
annotations.text: ◦ Specially they ſought to Peter the cheefe of al, vvho not onely by touching, as the other, but by his very ſhadovv cured al diſeaſes. vvhere vpon S. Auguſtine ſaith, If then the ſhadovv of his body could helpe, hovv much more novv the fulnes of povver? And if then a certaine litle vvind of him paſſing by did profite them that humbly aſked, hovv much more the grace of him novv being permanent & remaining? Ser. 29. de Sanctis, ſpeaking of the miracles done by the Saincts novv reigning in heauen.
